scope: Parent-owned timeout feasibility only. No launcher, worker tools, or production architecture enabled.
reader: ABU-392 reviewers checking which capabilities have evidence and which remain unproved.
probeRequirements: Run from this checkout in an authorized herdr pane with Node, Pi, and herdr installed. The probe creates an isolated server and retains its temporary evidence directory.

capabilities.name: Canonical Pi recognition and input
capabilities.method: herdr agent start for both parent and worker, explicit installed herdr Pi integration, isolated Pi resources, and offline startup. Herdr reported Pi with interactive_ready=true and the expected session path. Local slash commands wrote acceptance files; native user bash wrote a child PID file.
capabilities.limits: No model turn was requested. Readiness, command acceptance, task output, and stopped work are separate observations. The probe does not use agent prompt --wait for model-free commands.

capabilities.name: Parent-active Pi worker timeout
capabilities.method: The parent Pi owns a 5000 ms monotonic deadline with 2000 ms reserved for cancellation. After identity checks, one herdr agent send-keys call sends Ctrl+C then Ctrl+D. The probe confirms the Pi PID is absent, its shell is foreground, and its ordinary native user-bash child is absent.
capabilities.limits: Pi uses its default clear/exit bindings and editor. Custom keymaps, modal UIs, model streaming, and arbitrary detached descendants are not proved. Ctrl+C alone is not Pi cancellation. Parent event-loop and OS scheduling can delay attempts; this is not a real-time guarantee.

capabilities.name: Ordinary foreground process cancellation
capabilities.method: A real Node foreground fixture receives one identity-checked herdr pane send-keys Ctrl+C. Confirmation requires both an absent owned PID and the original shell in the foreground.
capabilities.limits: This check alone does not prove Pi cancellation. A surviving or reused PID prevents confirmed cleanup. Background or detached descendants are not contained.

capabilities.name: Bounded failed and stalled client attempts
capabilities.method: After real identity inspection, inject a herdr client pointed at a nonexistent isolated socket, then a stalled Node client. Each cancellation attempt shares a 300 ms budget. Both return unconfirmed cleanup and a manual cleanup target while the ordinary worker remains alive. A later healthy cancellation confirms cleanup.
capabilities.limits: These are injected client failures, not server-crash tests. The client timeout stops waiting and kills only the owned client process. No cancellation independent of herdr availability is claimed. Scheduling adds measurement overhead.

capabilities.name: Owned identity and unrelated work
capabilities.method: Check the pane, shell PID, foreground PID, and unique launch argument before sending keys. Pi additionally requires the recognized Pi session path. Unit checks refuse replaced PIDs, changed launch arguments, and missing identity. A live mismatched token leaves the ordinary fixture alive. The parent Pi remains alive after worker cancellation.
capabilities.limits: Inspection and input delivery are not atomic. Concurrent pane reassignment or replacement between those calls is not protected by a compare-and-stop API. Use only exclusively owned local panes; this is not an adversarial identity or permission boundary.

capabilities.name: Fixed deadline across activity and reconnect
capabilities.method: Fake timers prove one cancellation and one result Promise. Real parent Pi activity and reconnect commands observe the same task handle, parent PID, and deadline. A fake-clock regression advances beyond the deadline and proves no late cancellation call is made.
capabilities.limits: Reconnect means observing the same in-memory task while the parent runs. There is no relaunch, resubmission, native resume, reload recovery, or newly granted budget. An expired budget reports unconfirmed cleanup.

capabilities.name: Evidence after parent exit
capabilities.method: After parent Pi exits, the probe reads the previously written timeout result and partial evidence unchanged. Fake timers prove parent shutdown ends pending observation without later cancellation calls.
capabilities.limits: Saved evidence is not active enforcement. No controller, deadline, or reporting promise survives parent exit. This slice does not classify completed task reports or implement protected reporting.

capabilities.name: macOS compatibility
capabilities.method: Source inspection finds Node timers, AbortSignal, child_process, POSIX signals, and herdr terminal input available on Linux and macOS. Herdr has native foreground-job and argv implementations for both systems. The retained code uses no systemd, /proc parsing, Linux-only process wrapper, or independent supervisor.
capabilities.limits: No macOS runtime test ran. Run both retained checks on macOS with the recorded Pi/herdr versions before claiming runtime support. Check canonical startup/input, default Pi clear/exit behavior, foreground identity, client budgets, process exit, and evidence retention there.
